<document id=DOC_excerpt_settle_order>
DISCOUNT_BY_TIER = {"standard": 20, "premium": 30}

def settle_order(account_tier, total_amount, coupon_codes, coupon_lookup):
    discount = DISCOUNT_BY_TIER[account_tier]
    coupon_sum = coupon_lookup[coupon_codes[0]]
    amount_owed = total_amount * discount / 100 - coupon_sum
    return amount_owed
</document>

The module below redeems coupon codes by looking them up. Nothing in
it limits how long a code stays redeemable, so every code ever issued
remains valid indefinitely.

Recommend how the design should bound a code's lifetime, and say what
the lookup would have to carry for that bound to be enforceable.

response.text:
Bound each code with an absolute expiry, and make the lookup return that expiry alongside the value so redemption can reject it.

Give every issued code a fixed `expires_at` (UTC), set when the code is created — for example issue time plus a TTL, or a campaign end date. Do not infer lifetime from the code string or from the client. A code is redeemable only while server time is strictly before `expires_at`. After that it is invalid even if it is still in the table.

`coupon_lookup` cannot stay a map from code to a bare number. It has to carry at least:

- the discount value
- `expires_at`

Redemption must read both, compare `expires_at` to authoritative server time, and only then apply the value. If the lookup still returns only a number, nothing in `settle_order` can enforce a lifetime.
